reference.source: GeneReviews / Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: An autosomal dominant disorder caused by haploinsufficiency of MYCN, from either a loss-of-function variant or a deletion
Microcephaly is a consistent feature and is often the finding that prompts genetic evaluation
Characteristic digital anomalies include brachymesophalangy, clinodactyly of the fifth finger, and syndactyly of the toes
Gastrointestinal atresias, particularly oesophageal and duodenal atresia, are a hallmark and important surgical concern
Learning difficulties are common but many individuals have normal or only mildly reduced intellect
Short palpebral fissures and other subtle facial features may be present
The combination of microcephaly with digital and gastrointestinal anomalies should raise the diagnosis
Diagnosis is by identifying a MYCN variant or a deletion encompassing MYCN on microarray
reference.pathophysiology: Feingold syndrome type 1 arises from haploinsufficiency of MYCN, a transcription factor of the MYC family that drives cell proliferation and is critical during embryonic development of the limbs, gut, brain, and other organs. Reduced MYCN dosage, whether from an intragenic loss-of-function variant or a deletion of the gene, impairs the proliferative programmes it normally coordinates, resulting in microcephaly, the characteristic hand and foot anomalies, and failure of normal luminal development in the gut that produces oesophageal and duodenal atresia. Because the mechanism is loss of one functional copy, the disorder is inherited in an autosomal dominant manner, with variable expression among affected individuals.
additionalDifferentials: VACTERL association with overlapping gastrointestinal and limb anomalies
CHARGE syndrome with atresia and multiple congenital anomalies
Other syndromic causes of microcephaly with digital anomalies
Fanconi anaemia with limb anomalies and growth restriction
Isolated oesophageal or duodenal atresia of non-syndromic cause
Feingold syndrome type 2 due to a different genetic mechanism
additionalInvestigations: Molecular testing of MYCN, together with microarray to detect a deletion
Imaging and surgical assessment of suspected oesophageal or duodenal atresia
Hand and foot radiography to characterise digital anomalies
Serial head circumference measurement and neuroimaging where indicated
Renal and cardiac evaluation for associated anomalies
redFlags: Neonatal oesophageal atresia with aspiration risk requiring urgent surgery
Duodenal atresia presenting with bilious vomiting in the newborn
Feeding failure and faltering growth related to gastrointestinal anomaly
Significant associated cardiac or renal malformation
reference.prognosis: With timely surgical correction of gastrointestinal atresias, the long-term outlook is generally good and lifespan is usually normal; most individuals have normal or mildly reduced intellect, and the microcephaly and digital anomalies are non-progressive, so the principal early risk relates to the neonatal management of the atresias.
pitfalls: Managing an isolated oesophageal or duodenal atresia without recognising the underlying syndrome
Overlooking microcephaly as a diagnostic clue when digital anomalies are subtle
Relying on sequencing alone and missing a whole-gene deletion detectable on microarray
Assuming intellectual disability is invariable when many individuals have normal cognition
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
management: Arrange prompt neonatal surgical correction of oesophageal or duodenal atresia, the principal early surgical concern
Provide developmental support with early educational and learning intervention for associated learning difficulties
Undertake serial head circumference monitoring and neuroimaging where clinically indicated given the consistent microcephaly
Evaluate for and manage associated renal and cardiac anomalies
Offer orthopaedic and hand assessment of digital anomalies such as brachymesophalangy and syndactyly, intervening only where function is limited
Coordinate multidisciplinary follow-up across clinical genetics, paediatric surgery and developmental services
Provide genetic counselling and offer family screening with molecular testing of relatives given the autosomal dominant MYCN haploinsufficiency
